title: A store drawn from its prospectus
label: Brand gallery
lede: We found no freely licensed photograph of a Zany Brainy store, and we did not capture the archived website for this page. These are our own drawings, based on how the company described its stores to investors. They are not official artwork.

drawings.title: The store.
drawings.caption: The chain put its stores mainly in suburban strip and power shopping centers.[^3] Original illustration; the sign lettering is deliberately blank.

drawings.title: The reading area.
drawings.caption: Carpet, low shelving and a place to sit and read, as the prospectus describes.[^1] Original illustration.

drawings.title: The tower.
drawings.caption: From 103 stores to 188 in one fiscal year.[^2][^3] Original illustration.

drawings.title: The sale.
drawings.caption: December 2003: liquidators sell the inventory of the last 89 stores.[^17][^25] Original illustration, not a photograph of a real store.

blocks.title: The same store, 1999 and 2003

before.caption: The IPO year: 103 stores and a profit.[^2]
before.alt: Drawing of a colorful toy store open for business

after.label: December 2003
after.caption: Eighty-nine stores, all to be liquidated.[^25]
after.alt: Drawing of the same store during a liquidation sale

blocks.source: Both panels are original illustrations, not photographs. Store counts: fiscal 1999 annual report[^2] and Publishers Weekly[^25].

disclaimer: The colors are our own choice for the drawings and were not sampled from the company’s logo or stores. Zany Brainy, Noodle Kidoodle, The Right Start and FAO Schwarz are trademarks of their owners and are discussed here in historical and editorial context.
